objectives: Segment short /i/ CVC words into phonemes.
Map each phoneme to the correct grapheme and spell the word.
Use read-back to verify short /i/ spelling.
concepts: Encoding moves from spoken sounds to written graphemes.
Short /i/ must be preserved in the middle position during spelling.
Minimal contrasts expose vowel spelling errors.

definitions.definition: Representing spoken phonemes with written graphemes.
Separating a spoken word into its individual phonemes.
Reading a newly written word to check whether it matches the intended word.

workedExamples: sat for sit → compare the middle phoneme and replace a with i.
commonMistakes: Writing without first segmenting the word.

basic: Spell sit, pin and tin from dictation.
conceptual: Identify the vowel causing an encoding error.
higherOrderThinking: Choose the correction step that matches an i/a spelling error.
mixedReview: Spell short /a/ and /i/ CVC words and compare.

mistakeBasedRevision: sit → sat error: check the middle vowel.
pin → pan error: check the middle vowel.
weakTopicRevision: Practise i/a minimal pairs before spelling the full word again.

outcomes: Learner segments short /i/ CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner spells short /i/ CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner represents short /i/ with i in the middle position.
Learner uses read-back to detect and correct an encoding error.

questions.question: Which word has i in the middle?
What should you do first when spelling a spoken CVC word?
options: Say it and segment its sounds

questions.question: After segmenting /s/ /i/ /t/, what should you do?
options: Map each sound to a grapheme and write it

questions.question: A learner writes “sat” for “sit.” Which sound needs checking?
A learner writes “pan” for “pin.” What should be checked?
Why should the learner read the written word back?
options: To check that the graphemes represent the intended sounds

questions.question: Which spelling has short /i/ in the middle?
Which contrast helps check short /i/ spelling?
Which spelling begins p, has short /i/, and ends n?
What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Encode taught CVC words with short /i/ accurately
